title: A worker hung on a dropped connection burns its whole wall clock
description:
DIAGNOSED LIVE, 2026-09-22. Two pi workers - keh on epic-xte and w9b on epic-wne - sat for 26 and 38 minutes having produced nothing, and would have burned their full 3600s wall clock. The cause was the same for both and it is not the model.

THE EVIDENCE, in the order it settled the question:
  - Both processes ALIVE, state SN, 0.0% CPU, ~9-11 seconds of CPU total across the
    whole run. Doing nothing, not spinning.
  - Each held exactly ONE established socket: TCP to 2606:4700:300a::... port 443 -
    Cloudflare. No other network activity, no child processes.
  - Cloudflare itself was healthy: curl to api.cloudflare.com answered in ~0.5s on both
    IPv4 and IPv6, so it was not a routing or IPv6 problem.
  - The MODEL was healthy: pi -p --model cloudflare-workers-ai/@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3
    'Reply with exactly: OK' returned OK immediately, while both workers were hung.
  - Neither worktree had a single uncommitted change or an unpushed commit.

So each worker's inference request was dropped in flight and the socket left half-open.
Nothing errored, so nothing retried, so pi waited forever. This correlates with the
transient network event the runs recorded at ~16:10 ('git ls-remote failed transiently:
Connection to 140.82.121.4 port 22 timed out') - the same blip that the run's own remote
retries survived because THEY have a timeout.

THIS IS A SHAPE THIS REPOSITORY HAS ALREADY BEEN BITTEN BY. jge was an 8-hour hang from
exactly it: curl --retry was added without a stall bound, and --retry only fires on
FAILURE, so a stalled-but-open connection never failed and never retried. The fix there
was --speed-limit 1024 --speed-time 120. Same disease, different client.

WHAT TO FIX, and it is two things that should not be confused:
  1. The REQUEST needs an idle bound. A connection that delivers no bytes for N seconds
     is dead and must be failed so the retry that already exists can fire. Whether that
     lives in pi's config or in what ticfac passes it is the work.
  2. TICFAC SHOULD NOT NEED (1) TO BE TRUE. The stall warning already saw this - 'alive
     but has produced nothing durable for 15m37s... has written NOTHING into its
     worktree since the run first looked at it' - and then did nothing, because it is
     explicitly 'a reason to look, not a verdict'. For an unattended factory there is
     nobody to look. A worker that has written NOTHING and is using NO CPU for a
     multiple of the heartbeat interval is not slow, it is hung, and the run can act on
     that without a person. Note this is distinct from a slow worker: CPU near zero AND
     zero bytes written is the conjunction that makes it safe to call.

WHAT I DID BY HAND, which is what the run should have done: killed each runner by exact
pid. Both supervisors immediately rejected with collect_failed / missing-result and the
runs moved on. Nothing was lost - neither attempt held any work.
acceptance_criteria: A worker whose connection is dropped mid-request fails within a bounded idle period rather than hanging to the wall clock; and independently, an unattended run interrupts an attempt that has produced no bytes and consumed no CPU for a bounded multiple of the heartbeat interval, without a person looking, recording why it judged the attempt hung rather than slow
